sources.title: A Control Architecture for Training-Free Memory Use
Beyond Retrieval: Query-Conditioned Reuse of Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories

observations.text: The TAG control-architecture paper explicitly separates retrieval exposure from applicability. Its memory-conditioned second pass is accepted only if it improves confidence by a margin and passes structural guards; otherwise the system rolls back to the baseline action. The locked training-free protocol reports +7.0 points on SVAMP and +7.67 on ASDiv over baseline, with smaller positive transfer to QA/agent tasks, and includes fixed-retrieval counterfactual analysis.

TAG is the closest causal precedent found so far for post-retrieval accept/reject control, but its main quantitative evidence is arithmetic/QA/agent rather than autonomous science, and acceptance is based on confidence/structural guards rather than a science-domain mechanism/assumption compatibility predicate.

Query-Conditioned Reuse (QCR) holds candidate retrieval, target state, model, decoding and tool budget fixed while varying how the same selected trajectory is delivered. Across 2,391 WebArena/WorkArena/AppWorld target instances, target-bound support with applicability conditions and verification requirements reaches 62.3% Success, 10.7 points above Full Trajectory while using 48.9% fewer online tokens.

QCR directly demonstrates that post-retrieval reuse can be causally isolated from retrieval quality, but it changes the representation/support delivered rather than holding one memory representation fixed and toggling only an applicability admission bit; it is also not science-domain evidence.

protocol_inferences.name: POST_RETRIEVAL_CONTROL_IS_A_SEPARATE_CAUSAL_AXIS
protocol_inferences.text: Evaluation should hold retrieval/candidate identity fixed when claiming benefit from receiver-side reuse/admission control; otherwise retrieval quality and applicability control remain confounded.

protocol_inferences.name: REJECTED_MEMORY_MUST_ROLL_BACK_OR_ABSTAIN
protocol_inferences.text: A receiver rejection should have an explicit operational consequence: roll back to an independently valid baseline action or preserve empty memory. It must not silently fall through to forced memory injection.

phase1_acceptance.reason: Both systems use model inference/tool execution and do not provide a zero-dependency scheduled-Chat completion mechanism. They are causal/mechanism evidence for separating retrieval from reuse/admission only.

scope_notes: Do not generalize TAG's arithmetic gains into science-domain performance claims.
Do not claim QCR isolates an accept/reject gate; it isolates target-conditioned representation/use with retrieval held fixed.
Neither source closes the requested science-domain fixed-record receiver-applicability ablation frontier.
